newsitem.title: BRAZIL: No Brazil coffee council meeting today.
newsitem.headline: No Brazil coffee council meeting today.

text.p: There will be no meeting of Brazil's CDPC coffee council Thursday, a Ministry of Industry and Commerce spokeswoman said.

Quoting Roberto Abreu, interim head of the National Coffee Department, the spokeswoman said there was also no guarantee that Ministry of Industry and Commerce officials will meet with their Finance Ministry colleagues next week.
The meetings had been called to thrash out an agreement on lending stocks to the soluble coffee industry, which is complaining that it will soon have to import coffee to meet production demands.

Industry sources said the plan had been put on hold while the two ministries battled over it. Why the Finance Ministry should be opposing lending coffee stocks to the soluble industry was not immediately clear.
The soluble industry agreed to delay importing coffee until the CDPC, which groups the private and public sector and is supposed to define national coffee policy, had worked out a solution.
A date for the next formal CDPC meeting, expected to take place in Santos, has yet to be announced.
